frontier.hypothesis: The scaled-offset attractor (tail-correct, 8/92) is one load-delay nop and one sunk lbu away from target, which is a strictly smaller residual than the candidate's - a lever that separates its adjacent arg5 lw/sw pair would convert it to 8/91 and possibly below.
frontier.mechanism: Target separates the arg5 load from its 16($sp) store by six instructions (the D_800A11D5 chain sits between them), so no load-delay nop is needed. In the scaled-offset form store_one_arg emits lw and sw adjacently and the scheduler does not separate them, costing one instruction. The candidate chassis DOES separate them (lw at 52, sw at 55), so the separation is reachable in principle - it is the arg4 spelling that decides whether the D_800A11D5 chain lands between them.
frontier.next_probe: On the scaled-offset chassis only, sweep spellings that force the D_800A11D5/arg3 chain to be emitted between arg5's load and its store: arg3 as a named value, as a named address, as its own scaled offset, and each crossed with the arg3 statement placed before / between / after the k0 statement. The 78-form cross-product only measured arg3 as {inline, named value} and only with arg3's statement last. Use tmp/grind/CD_datasync/s21 (0.5 s/form) and read the result with cmp.py 40 60 rather than by score alone - the informative signal is whether the D5 chain moves between build idx of the arg5 lw and the sw.

frontier.hypothesis: F32 (inherited, unchanged) - tools/ra_solver/inverse.py local can type the block-3 seat residual REACHABLE or FORECLOSED and name the C-lever vectors, converting this function's disposition from an exhaustion argument into a proof.
frontier.mechanism: s20's classify verdict names inverse.py as the next tool and extracted the QTYDBG attribution (block 3 quantities, births, deaths, refs, allocation order, reproduced qty_compare priorities). find_free_reg's ascending scan gives a closed-form condition for target's $a0 seat: both $v0 and $v1 occupied across the chain's whole span at allocation time. s21 re-confirmed from the emission side that the register difference is downstream of the ordering - the candidate's idx[0] chain is live 41-49 (so $v0 is free) while target's is live 41-56 (so it is not).
frontier.next_probe: Run inverse.py local against CD_datasync block 3 with a HAND-VERIFIED --goal-order (perturb.py --goal-from-target still SKIPS this block: 'goal is not a topological order, 2 violations', because difflib mis-pairs the duplicate sll / lw skeletons; anchor-based alignment is an operator-lane change to tools/). Bound and profile the run - the CD_ready precedent is that an unbounded inverse.py local can burn 100% CPU without finishing depth 1. A REACHABLE verdict must name a lever vector nobody has spelled; the banked count is now 96 rejected forms plus this session's 86 measured spellings.

frontier.hypothesis: The standing family trigger (inherited, unchanged) - a JOINT sched.c-emission-order x global.c/local-alloc.c-seat solver closes CD_datasync, CD_sync and CD_ready together.
frontier.mechanism: Every C change that fixes the emission order breaks the register seats and vice versa - proven over 21 sessions here, 68 on CD_ready and 107 on CD_sync. s21 adds the sharpest instance yet: the scaled-offset geometry buys target's entire tail and pays for it with the block head, and the named-value geometry does the exact reverse. The current solver suite is single-axis, which is why all three twins land on the same disposition.
frontier.next_probe: When a joint solver exists, re-open CD_datasync, CD_sync and CD_ready as ONE basin. Use the s21 harness (tmp/grind/CD_datasync/s21/, ~0.5 s/form, calibrated sandbox = lev + nop - 3, function-agnostic apart from the hardcoded name) as the scoring loop - it supersedes the s19 dual-fork harness, which was nop-blind.
